newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Vendex and BIS shares suspended amid bid talk.
newsitem.headline: Vendex and BIS shares suspended amid bid talk.

text.p: Trading in shares of Dutch retail and business services group Vendex International NV and French temporary employment agency Bis were suspended on Monday amid market talk that Vendex was about to launch a takeover bid for BIS.
Vendex declined to make any comment about the reason for the suspension but said it would issue a statement later today and hold a news conference at 1330 GMT.
BIS shares were suspended on December 30 following the death of the company's founder and chairman Laurent Negro but trade in the shares is due to start again on Tuesday.
A spokesman told Reuters last week that BIS -- France's third biggest temporary help agency after Adecco and Manpower -- would continue to seek an international business partner.
Vendex derived 1.9 billion guilders ($1.09 billion) of its total 1995/96 turnover of 11.3 billion guilders from temporary help services.
Its Vedior temporary help unit is mainly active in the Benelux countries but ranks fifth in France and also operates in Spain and Germany.

Vendex raised 484 million guilders in October by selling shares in Dutch retail group KBB. Analysts said at the time they expected this money to be reinvested by means of an acquisition in the area of business services.
Critics have said BIS has focused too much on France and has been left behind in the trend towards globalisation. The company had a turnover of 9.2 billion french francs ($1.76 billion) in 1995.
